hook: Why does inserting into a binary search tree always come back out sorted?

narration.text: Every new value starts at the root and walks down until it finds an empty spot.
50 becomes the root — the very first node has nothing to compare against yet.
30 and 70 each compare once against the root, landing left and right immediately.
20 compares against 50, then 30, before finally attaching to 30's empty left.
40 follows the same path as 20 until the values diverge, then attaches right of 30.
65 and 80 both walk past 50 and 70 before settling into their own empty slots.
Reading the finished tree left, node, right in order hands back a perfectly sorted list.

youtube.title: Binary Search Tree Insertion, Visually
youtube.description: How inserting values one at a time into a binary search tree — each walking down from the root to find its slot — always leaves the tree readable back out in sorted order.
